structures.title: The basic statement (SVO)
structures.explanation: Mandarin's core order is the same as English: subject, then verb, then object. The verb never changes form for person or tense. This is the frame every other pattern builds on.

structures.title: Placing time and location
structures.explanation: Time and place go BEFORE the verb, not after it as in English. Time usually comes before place. This order is fixed and marks fluent word order.
structures.ex2_ref: He has an exam at school tomorrow.

structures.title: Yes/no questions
structures.explanation: Turn any statement into a yes/no question by adding 吗 at the end. Word order does not change at all. The answer repeats the verb (去/不去) rather than 'yes/no'.

structures.title: 'What about X?' questions
structures.explanation: 呢 attaches to a noun to ask 'and what about X?' without repeating the whole question. It reuses the context already established. Very common for bouncing a question back.

structures.title: Completed action with 了
structures.explanation: Put 了 after the verb to mark that the action is completed. It is about completion or change, not strictly past tense. Habitual actions do not take 了.

structures.pattern: 想 / 要 / 可以 + Verb
structures.title: Want to / will / can + verb
structures.explanation: These modal verbs sit directly before the main verb: 想 (would like to), 要 (want/will), 可以 (may/can). They express desire, intention, or permission without changing the main verb.
structures.ex1_ref: I want to go to Beijing.

structures.title: Making comparisons
structures.explanation: Compare two things with 比: A is more [adjective] than B. Do not add 很 before the adjective. For the negative use A + 没有 + B + adjective.
structures.ex1_ref: Apples are more expensive than oranges.
structures.ex2_ref: My younger brother is taller than me.

structures.title: Emphasizing how/when/where
structures.explanation: Use 是...的 to highlight the time, place, or manner of a known past action. 是 goes before the detail you stress and 的 closes the sentence. It answers 'it was [when/where/how] that...'.
structures.ex1_ref: It was yesterday that he came.

structures.title: Existence with 有
structures.explanation: 有 states that something exists at a location: Place + 有 + Noun. Negate with 没有, never 不有. It answers 'there is / there are'.
structures.ex1_ref: There is a book on the table.
structures.ex2_ref: There are twenty students in our class.

structures.title: Relative clauses with 的
structures.explanation: A whole descriptive phrase plus 的 goes BEFORE the noun it modifies — the opposite of English 'who/that' clauses that follow the noun. 的 links the description to the noun.

structures.pattern: 因为 + Clause + 所以 + Clause
structures.title: Because... therefore...
structures.explanation: Chinese keeps both halves of the pair: 因为 introduces the reason, 所以 introduces the result. Unlike English, using both words together is natural and common.
structures.ex1_ref: Because it's raining, I'm not going.
structures.ex2_target: 因为很累，所以他早点睡了。
structures.ex2_ref: Because he was tired, he went to bed early.

structures.title: Obligation with 得 (děi)
structures.explanation: 得 (read děi) before a verb means 'must / have to'. It expresses necessity. Its negation is 不用 (need not), not 不得.
structures.ex2_ref: I have to get up early tomorrow.

structures.title: The passive voice
structures.explanation: 被 marks the passive: the subject receives the action, optionally naming the agent after 被. The verb needs an extra element (了 or a complement). It often implies something unwanted.
structures.ex2_ref: The cake was eaten by my younger brother.

structures.title: The superlative with 最
structures.explanation: Put 最 before an adjective to mean 'the most' / '-est'. Often ends with 的 when describing a noun. No article or extra word is needed.
structures.ex2_ref: This restaurant is the most delicious.

structures.title: Ongoing action (progressive)
structures.explanation: 正在 before the verb shows an action in progress right now, like English '-ing'. You may also add 呢 at the end for emphasis. It stresses that the action is happening at this moment.
structures.ex2_ref: He is on the phone right now.

structures.pattern: 虽然 + Clause + 但是 + Clause
structures.title: Although... still...
structures.explanation: 虽然 sets up a concession and 但是 introduces the contrasting result. As with 因为...所以, Chinese keeps both connectors. It means 'although X, nevertheless Y'.
structures.ex1_ref: Although it's raining, I still go.
structures.ex2_ref: Although it's expensive, it's very tasty.
